{{Short description|British physicist (1930–2019)}}
'''Charles William Trowbridge''' (10 July 1930 – 13 November 2019) was a British physicist and engineer working in the field of [[computational electromagnetics]].

==Career==
Trowbridge was born on 10 July 1930 in [[Totton and Eling|Totton]].<ref name="KaaKaa2008">{{cite book|author1=D. J. van de Kaa|author2=Kaa|author3=Y. de Roo|title=De Leden Van de Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie Van Wetenschappen: Een Demografisch Perspectief: 1808 Tot 2008|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gzNvCGJEGCYC&pg=PA348|date=19 December 2008|publisher=Amsterdam University Press|isbn=978-90-6984-552-4|page=348}}</ref> From 1946 to 1948 he received naval training on ''[[HMS Conway (school ship)|HMS Conway]]''. He subsequently worked eight years in the [[merchant navy]].<ref name=guardian>{{cite web|author=Simon Trowbridge |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2020/jan/16/bill-trowbridge-obituary |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200229173500/https://www.theguardian.com/science/2020/jan/16/bill-trowbridge-obituary |title=Bill Trowbridge obituary |publisher=The Guardian |date=16 January 2020 |archive-date=29 February 2020}}</ref> From 1957 to 1961 he worked at the [[Atomic Energy Research Establishment]].<ref name="GroßWestermann2007">{{cite book|author1=Dominik Groß|author2=Stefanie Westermann|title=Vom Bild zur Erkenntnis?: Visualisierungskonzepte in den Wissenschaften|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=o4nUR5leNZ4C&pg=PA175|year=2007|publisher=kassel university press GmbH|isbn=978-3-89958-342-7|page=175}}</ref>  During this period he obtained a degree in physics from [[University of Westminster|Regent Street Polytechnic]].<ref name=scw>{{cite web|author=John Murphy |url=https://www.scientific-computing.com/feature/no-substitute-experience |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200702212421/https://www.scientific-computing.com/feature/no-substitute-experience |title=No substitute for experience |publisher=Scientific Computing World |date=1 December 2006 |archive-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>

Trowbridge started working at the [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory|Rutherford Laboratory]] in 1961. In 1971 he became head of its Computing Applications Group. When the Compumag conferences started in 1976 he was the first chairperson.<ref name="GroßWestermann2007"/> In 1984 he was co-founder of Vector Fields Ltd, a computer aided engineering consultancy.<ref name="GroßWestermann2007"/><ref>{{cite web|author=John Simkin |url=https://www.ercim.eu/publication/Ercim_News/enw24/vector.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417205712/http://www.ercim.eu/publication/Ercim_News/enw24/vector.html |title=What are Vector Fields? |publisher=Ercim News |date=January 1996 |archive-date=17 April 2016}}</ref> Trowbridge served as head of the company until it was bought by Chelton in 2005.<ref name="GroßWestermann2007"/><ref name=scw/> In 1987 he retired from the Rutherford Laboratory.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.chilton-computing.org.uk/inf/eng/electromagnetics/overview.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170601235657/http://www.chilton-computing.org.uk/inf/eng/electromagnetics/overview.htm |title=Electromagnetics |publisher=chilton-computing.org.uk |date= |archive-date=1 June 2017}}</ref> Apart from his other positions he was a visiting professor at [[King's College London]].<ref name=guardian/><ref name=knaw>{{cite web|author= |url=https://knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/4883 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200426081638/https://knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/4883 |title=Bill Trowbridge |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=26 April 2020}}</ref> Trowbridge is considered to be one of the founders of the field of [[computational electromagnetics]].<ref name=scw/>

Trowbridge was elected a foreign member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1992.<ref name=knaw/> In 1993 he was made Officer in the [[Order of the British Empire]].<ref name=guardian/>

He died on 13 November 2019, aged 89.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/announcements/deaths/deaths/18057719.Bill_TROWBRIDGE/ |title=Bill Trowbridge |publisher=Oxford Mail |date=25 November 2019 |access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>
